_comment: THE REVIEWED DESTINATION POLICY for the PostgreSQL copy fence.
Read by pg-copy-ops.ts via --destination-policy. Every reviewed label must
appear exactly once, in the reviewed order, and each entry DECLARES two facts
that the census then COMPARES against what it measured:
installation - the STABLE topology: is this agent installed at all?
expected     - which database it writes to, if any
Neither is inferred. A census that measured something the policy did not
declare refuses.
THIS POLICY DOES NOT SAY WHETHER AN INSTALLED AGENT IS CURRENTLY LOADED.
That is deliberate, and it is what S4F-D5-K5.3 corrected. `installed-loaded`,
`installed-disabled` and `installed-unloaded` are observations about launchd,
not installation topologies, and they change during the very sequence this
policy has to survive: the rehearsal needs every producer STOPPED, and the
restoration needs them BACK. A destination policy naming `installed-unloaded`
refused after the operator restored the agents; one naming `installed-loaded`
refused before. Either way the operational binding digest moved, and
--verify-restoration then rejected the restored world as a different world
from the one the rehearsal was taken against - so a proved rehearsal could
never reach its own review.
The phase-specific facts belong to the documents that own them: the quiescence
census proves the producers stopped before and while fenced, and the
post-restoration policy requires daily/watchdog/alerts loaded-scheduled-healthy
and worker running afterwards.
CURRENT STATE: the four production plists are installed under
~/Library/LaunchAgents, so each declares `installed` and, because each names
the pipeline credential container, `writes-copy-source`. The structured worker
is not installed on this machine at all - no label and no plist - so it is
`expected-absent` in both columns, and every one of its evidence fields is
null by contract.
